knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The stripping sequence starts at the outside edges so the edging is handled before the open floor. Working from the middle or the doorway is not in the procedure.
Slurry left to dry is harder to remove and can leave marks on the bare floor, which is why it must be picked up while wet.
A taped lead and a lapsed test date both fail the equipment check. The machine is tagged out and reported. The operator does not repair, re-tape, or add a protective device.

practicalCriteria: Learner inspects a supplied buffer and wet pick-up, identifies a planted fault such as a taped lead or torn blade, and tags the machine out of service.
Learner marks the working sequence on a supplied floor plan: outside edges first, sections small enough to clear while wet, slurry picked up before it dries.
Learner applies a practice polish coat to a practice panel edge first and cross-weaves a second coat after the first has dried, observed by the assessor.
Learner stores the buffer upright with the pad and base plate removed, and the wet pick-up washed, blade wiped and float rinsed.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Completed equipment check record with any tagged-out item
Assessor observation record for the practice polish panel
stopWorkCriteria: Electrical lead damaged, or electrical test status unknown or lapsed
Slurry or polish about to dry on an unprotected floor and the section cannot be cleared in time
Ventilation not available and the product label requires it
Any person enters the barrier while the floor is wet or unprotected
